choices.B: The SQL code must be rewritten in Python because Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines only supports Python definitions
choices.C: The streaming source must be converted to a batch source before migrating to Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines
choices.D: The Python code must be rewritten in SQL because Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines only supports SQL definitions

questions.shortAnswer: No changes are required.
questions.explanation: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines natively supports both Python and SQL within the same pipeline. It supports the medallion architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold layers) and handles streaming sources directly. The existing language mix and multi-hop architecture can migrate to Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines without modification to the underlying logic.

questions.title: Persist to Memory and Disk
questions.question: Which Spark method persists data to both memory and disk when memory is insufficient?

choices.A: `cache()` with `StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY`
choices.B: `persist()` with `StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK`
choices.C: `checkpoint()` with eager evaluation
choices.D: `broadcast()` with local storage fallback

questions.shortAnswer: `persist()` with `StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK`.
questions.explanation: `persist()` allows specifying a `StorageLevel` such as `MEMORY_AND_DISK`, which stores partitions in memory and spills excess to disk when memory is exhausted. `cache()` is a shortcut for `persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)` and does not spill to disk automatically.

questions.title: Broadcast Join for a Small Dimension *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A 2 TB `sales` DataFrame is joined to a 15 MB `stores` DataFrame on `store_id`. The Spark UI shows a `SortMergeJoin` with a large shuffle of `sales`. Which change avoids shuffling the large side?

choices.A: `sales.repartition(1).join(stores, "store_id")`
choices.B: `sales.crossJoin(stores).filter("sales.store_id = stores.store_id")`
choices.C: `sales.join(broadcast(stores), "store_id")`
choices.D: Lower `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` to 10

questions.shortAnswer: `sales.join(broadcast(stores), "store_id")`.
questions.explanation: `broadcast()` marks the small DataFrame for a broadcast join, which copies it to every executor so `sales` isn't shuffled. Its size (15 MB) is above the default `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` of 10 MB, which is why Spark didn't broadcast it automatically. A cross join multiplies rows. One partition removes parallelism. Fewer shuffle partitions don't remove the shuffle ([SQL performance tuning](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-performance-tuning.html)).

questions.title: union vs unionByName *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Two DataFrames hold the same columns in a different order: `df_a(id, name, city)` and `df_b(city, id, name)`. Which call combines them, keeping duplicate rows and matching columns correctly?

choices.A: `df_a.union(df_b)`
choices.B: `df_a.join(df_b, "id", "outer")`
choices.C: `df_a.union(df_b).distinct()`
choices.D: `df_a.unionByName(df_b)`

questions.shortAnswer: `df_a.unionByName(df_b)`.
questions.explanation: `union` resolves columns **by position**, so it would put `city` values into `id`. `unionByName` resolves them **by name**. Both keep duplicates, which is SQL `UNION ALL` semantics. Add `.distinct()` for SQL `UNION` behaviour. `allowMissingColumns=True` fills columns missing from one side with nulls ([PySpark unionByName](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/python/reference/pyspark.sql/api/pyspark.sql.DataFrame.unionByName.html)).

questions.title: Splitting and Exploding Columns *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Silver table has a `tags` string column such as `"red,large,sale"`. Analysts need one row per tag. Which PySpark expression produces it?

choices.A: `df.withColumn("tag", F.explode(F.split("tags", ",")))`
choices.B: `df.withColumn("tag", F.split("tags", ","))`
choices.C: `df.withColumn("tag", F.flatten("tags"))`
choices.D: `df.groupBy("tags").agg(F.collect_list("tags"))`

questions.shortAnswer: `df.withColumn("tag", F.explode(F.split("tags", ",")))`.
questions.explanation: `split` turns the string into an array using a (regular expression) pattern. `explode` then emits one row per array element. `split` alone leaves one row with an array. `flatten` works on arrays of arrays, and `collect_list` does the opposite of what's needed ([PySpark split](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/api/python/reference/pyspark.sql/api/pyspark.sql.functions.split.html)).

questions.title: Fast Distinct Counts on Huge Tables *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A dashboard shows the number of distinct visitors per day over billions of events. An exact `COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id)` is too slow, and a small error is acceptable. Which function fits?

choices.A: `count_if(visitor_id IS NOT NULL)`
choices.B: `approx_count_distinct(visitor_id)`
choices.C: `sum(DISTINCT visitor_id)`
choices.D: `collect_set(visitor_id)`

questions.shortAnswer: `approx_count_distinct(visitor_id)`.
questions.explanation: `approx_count_distinct` estimates the number of distinct values with HyperLogLog++. Its default maximum relative standard deviation is 5 %, and the `relativeSD` argument can tighten it. `collect_set` would build huge arrays, and the other options compute something else ([approx_count_distinct](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/functions/approx_count_distinct)).

questions.title: Shuffle Partitions vs Default Parallelism *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A DataFrame `groupBy` on 40 MB of data runs 200 tiny tasks after the shuffle on classic compute. An engineer wants to tune the post-shuffle partition count and then re-measure. Which setting controls it?

choices.A: `spark.default.parallelism`
choices.B: `spark.executor.memory`
choices.C: `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`
choices.D: `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold`

questions.shortAnswer: `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`.
questions.explanation: It sets the number of partitions used when shuffling data for joins or aggregations in the DataFrame and SQL engine (default 200). On Databricks, setting it to `auto` lets Spark size it from the plan and the data. `spark.default.parallelism` applies to RDD operations, memory settings size the JVMs, and the broadcast threshold controls join strategy ([AQE](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/aqe), [Spark SQL tuning](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/sql-performance-tuning.html)).

questions.title: Choosing a Gold Object for a Busy Dashboard *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Two hundred users open a dashboard each morning that aggregates revenue by region from a large Silver table. Hourly freshness is acceptable. The team wants fast reads and doesn't want to maintain refresh code. Which Unity Catalog object should back the dashboard?

choices.A: A standard view over the Silver table
choices.B: A streaming table that appends Silver rows
choices.C: A temporary view created by the dashboard query
choices.D: A materialized view refreshed on a schedule

questions.shortAnswer: A materialized view refreshed on a schedule.
questions.explanation: A materialized view stores precomputed results and refreshes them (incrementally when possible) on a schedule or when upstream data changes, so reads are cheap. A view recomputes the aggregation on every query. Temporary views are session-scoped. Streaming tables append new rows and don't recompute an aggregate ([standalone materialized views](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/views/materialized)).

questions.title: Adding an Upstream Task to an Existing Job
questions.question: A data engineer executes a single-task job each morning. Upon discovering an upstream data issue, they must add a new notebook to run before the original task. What is the correct approach to set up this new upstream task?

choices.A: Create a new task in the existing Job, and then add the original task as a dependency of the new task
choices.B: Create a separate Job for the new notebook and schedule it to run 30 minutes before the original Job
choices.C: Clone the existing Job and add the new notebook as a second task in the clone
choices.D: Replace the original task's notebook with a wrapper notebook that runs both notebooks sequentially

questions.shortAnswer: Create a new task in the existing Job, and then add the original task as a dependency of the new task.
questions.explanation: In Databricks Jobs, task dependencies are defined by specifying which tasks a given task "depends on." To insert an upstream step, the new task should have no dependencies (runs first), and the original task should be configured to depend on the new task (runs after).

questions.title: Limiting Query Refresh Schedule Duration
questions.question: An engineering manager wants a query to refresh every minute for the first week after a project launch, with no compute costs after that week. What strategy ensures the query stops refreshing and generating costs beyond week one?

choices.A: Set the SQL warehouse to auto-stop after one week of total runtime
choices.B: Set the query's refresh schedule to end on a specific date in the query scheduler
choices.C: Manually cancel the refresh schedule at the end of the week
choices.D: Create a Databricks Job to disable the query refresh after seven days

questions.shortAnswer: Set the query's refresh schedule to end on a specific date in the query scheduler.
questions.explanation: Databricks SQL query schedulers support an optional end date/time, allowing the refresh to automatically stop once the date is reached. No manual intervention is needed after the initial setup.

questions.title: Programmatic Job Schedule Representation
questions.question: A data engineer manages a complex job schedule and wants to represent and submit it to other jobs programmatically rather than manually selecting values in the Databricks scheduling form. Which tool enables this?

choices.A: Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) YAML configuration
choices.B: Apache Airflow DAG definitions
choices.C: Cron syntax
choices.D: JSON job templates via the Databricks CLI

questions.shortAnswer: Cron syntax.
questions.explanation: Databricks Jobs support quartz cron expressions for scheduling. Cron strings are compact, human-readable, and can be programmatically constructed and submitted via the Jobs API or embedded in Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) YAML configuration files.

questions.title: Scheduling a Daily SQL Query Refresh
questions.question: An engineering manager reviews a query daily but currently reruns it manually and waits for results. What strategy guarantees the query results are refreshed daily automatically?

choices.A: Use a Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines pipeline with a daily trigger to refresh the query
choices.B: Create a Databricks Job that runs the query notebook on a daily cron schedule
choices.C: Set up an Apache Airflow DAG to trigger the query execution daily
choices.D: Schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the query's page in Databricks SQL

questions.shortAnswer: Schedule the query to refresh every 1 day from the query's page in Databricks SQL.
questions.explanation: Databricks SQL provides a built-in scheduler accessible directly from the query editor. Setting a recurring daily refresh interval ensures results are always up-to-date without manual intervention or external orchestration tools.

questions.title: When to Use "Depends On" for a Job Task
questions.question: In what situations should a data engineer choose a task in the "Depends On" field when creating a new Databricks Job task?

choices.A: When another task needs to successfully complete before the new task begins
choices.B: When the new task should only run if a previous task has completed successfully
choices.C: When the new task processes data from a different database than other tasks
choices.D: When the new task needs to run on a different cluster than other tasks

questions.shortAnswer: When another task needs to successfully complete before the new task begins.
questions.explanation: The "Depends On" field establishes execution order in a Databricks Job DAG. The new task will only start after all specified upstream tasks have completed successfully. With the default Run if condition (*All succeeded*), if a dependency fails the downstream task doesn't run and is marked `Upstream failed`.

questions.title: Branching on New Data *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: An ingestion task publishes the number of rows it loaded as a task value. The transformation tasks should run only when that number is greater than zero. Which Lakeflow Jobs feature implements this?

choices.A: A For each task over the task value
choices.B: An If/else condition task comparing `{{tasks.ingest.values.rows_loaded}} > 0`, with transformations depending on its `true` outcome
choices.C: A retry policy on the transformation task
choices.D: Setting max concurrent runs to 0 when no data arrives

questions.shortAnswer: An If/else condition task comparing `{{tasks.ingest.values.rows_loaded}} > 0`, with transformations depending on its `true` outcome.
questions.explanation: The If/else task evaluates a boolean expression on two operands (task values, job parameters, literals). Downstream tasks depend on its `(true)` or `(false)` outcome. `>` performs a numeric comparison ([If/else task](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/if-else)).

questions.title: Looping Over Tables *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: The same load notebook must run for 30 source tables, at most five at a time, without defining 30 tasks. Which configuration meets this?

choices.A: A single notebook task with `max_retries` set to 30
choices.B: Thirty notebook tasks with no dependencies
choices.C: A For each task with the table list as input, the notebook as the nested task, and concurrency set to 5
choices.D: A Run Job task pointing at itself

questions.shortAnswer: A For each task with the table list as input, the notebook as the nested task, and concurrency set to 5.
questions.explanation: For each runs one nested task once per input element, passing `{{input}}` (or `{{input.<key>}}`). Concurrency defaults to 1, and the nested task can't itself be a For each ([For each task](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/for-each)).

questions.title: Retrying Transient Failures *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A task that calls an external API fails a few times a week with transient network errors, and succeeds when re-run minutes later. What is the built-in way to handle this?

choices.A: Increase the task timeout
choices.B: Add an If/else task after it
choices.C: Set the job's max concurrent runs to 2
choices.D: Configure a retry policy on the task, with a retry interval

questions.shortAnswer: Configure a retry policy on the task, with a retry interval.
questions.explanation: Task-level retries automatically re-run a failed task after the configured interval. A timeout limits how long one attempt may run, and when both are set the timeout applies to each retry. Concurrency and branching don't retry anything ([Configure and edit tasks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-task)).

questions.title: Cleanup That Always Runs *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A job's final task drops temporary staging tables. It must run whether the upstream transform succeeds or fails. Which Run if condition should it use?

choices.A: All done
choices.B: At least one succeeded
choices.C: All succeeded
choices.D: All failed

questions.shortAnswer: All done.
questions.explanation: *All done* runs the task after all dependencies finish, whatever their status. The default, *All succeeded*, would mark the task `Upstream failed` and skip it when the transform fails. *All failed* runs it only after failures ([Configure task dependencies](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/conditional-tasks)).

questions.title: Processing Files Soon After Unpredictable Drops *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A partner uploads JSON files to a Unity Catalog external location at unpredictable times: sometimes several an hour, sometimes nothing for a day. Each drop should be processed shortly after it lands, without empty runs or idle compute. Which trigger should the Lakeflow Job use?

choices.A: Scheduled trigger every 5 minutes
choices.B: File arrival trigger on the external location
choices.C: Continuous trigger
choices.D: Manual trigger by an operator

questions.shortAnswer: File arrival trigger on the external location.
questions.explanation: A file arrival trigger monitors a UC external location or volume and starts a run only when new files appear. *Wait after last change* can batch bursts into one run. Polling schedules start runs that find nothing, and continuous triggers keep compute running ([file arrival triggers](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/file-arrival-triggers)).

questions.title: Running When Upstream Tables Change *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Gold build job must run after **both** `main.silver.orders` and `main.silver.customers` are updated. Those tables are maintained by two other teams' jobs, which run at varying times. Which trigger configuration fits?

choices.A: A scheduled trigger at 06:00
choices.B: A table update trigger on both tables with "Any table is updated"
choices.C: A table update trigger on both tables with "All tables are updated"
choices.D: A file arrival trigger on the tables' storage paths

questions.shortAnswer: A table update trigger on both tables with "All tables are updated".
questions.explanation: Table update triggers start a run when monitored UC tables change. With multiple tables, *Trigger when* can be set to **All tables are updated** or **Any table is updated**. The job's Run as principal needs `SELECT` on the tables. File arrival triggers can't target managed table locations ([table update triggers](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/trigger-table-update)).

questions.title: Time-Based vs Data-Driven Triggers *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A regulatory report must be published at exactly 07:00 every weekday, using whatever data has arrived by then. Which trigger fits best?

choices.A: Continuous trigger
choices.B: File arrival trigger
choices.C: Table update trigger
choices.D: Scheduled trigger with Quartz cron `0 0 7 ? * MON-FRI`

questions.shortAnswer: Scheduled trigger with Quartz cron `0 0 7 ? * MON-FRI`.
questions.explanation: When the deadline, not data availability, decides when work runs, a time-based schedule is right. Quartz cron puts seconds first, and `?` goes in day-of-month when day-of-week is constrained. Data-driven triggers fit when work should follow data arrival ([schedules and triggers](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/triggers)).

questions.title: Configuring a Dashboard Task *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: After a pipeline task refreshes Gold tables, an AI/BI dashboard must be refreshed in the same job. Which task configuration achieves this?

choices.A: A Dashboards task that depends on the pipeline task and uses a SQL warehouse
choices.B: A notebook task that calls `display()` on the Gold tables
choices.C: A For each task over the dashboard's widgets
choices.D: A second job with a scheduled trigger 30 minutes later

questions.shortAnswer: A Dashboards task that depends on the pipeline task and uses a SQL warehouse.
questions.explanation: Lakeflow Jobs has native task types for notebooks, SQL, dashboards, and pipelines. Making the Dashboards task depend on the pipeline task guarantees the order inside one DAG. A separate job on a fixed delay can run before the data is ready ([Configure and edit tasks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-task)).

questions.title: Passing a Value Between Tasks *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Task `ingest` computes the latest order date. Task `report` needs that value. Which code sets it in `ingest`?

choices.A: `dbutils.widgets.text("max_date", value)`
choices.B: `dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="max_date", value=value)`
choices.C: `spark.conf.set("max_date", value)`
choices.D: `dbutils.notebook.exit(value)` in every task

questions.shortAnswer: `dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set(key="max_date", value=value)`.
questions.explanation: Task values pass small, JSON-serializable results (up to 48 KiB) between tasks. Downstream tasks read them with `dbutils.jobs.taskValues.get(taskKey="ingest", key="max_date")` or, preferably, the reference `{{tasks.ingest.values.max_date}}` in parameters ([task values](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/task-values)).

questions.title: Reading Quartz Cron *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Lakeflow Job schedule uses the Quartz expression `0 30 2 * * ?`. When does it run?

choices.A: Every 30 minutes past 2 o'clock, every hour
choices.B: At 00:30 on the 2nd of every month
choices.C: At 02:30:00 every day
choices.D: Every 2 minutes at second 30

questions.shortAnswer: At 02:30:00 every day.
questions.explanation: Quartz fields are seconds, minutes, hours, day-of-month, month, day-of-week, and an optional year. So `0 30 2 * * ?` means second 0, minute 30, hour 2, every day of every month, with no specific day-of-week ([Quartz CronTrigger tutorial](https://www.quartz-scheduler.org/documentation/quartz-2.3.0/tutorials/crontrigger.html)).

questions.title: Where Pull Requests Are Created
questions.question: A data engineer works on a feature branch in a Databricks Git folder. Which step of their workflow is performed in the Git provider (for example GitHub) rather than in the Databricks Git dialog?

choices.A: Committing and pushing changes
choices.B: Creating the feature branch
choices.C: Pulling a teammate's latest changes
choices.D: Creating and merging the pull request into the default branch

questions.shortAnswer: Creating and merging the pull request into the default branch.
questions.explanation: Git folders handle branch creation, switching, Commit & Push, pull, merge, rebase, and conflict resolution in the workspace UI. The docs say to "use your Git provider's interface to create a pull request and merge it into the default branch", where reviews and branch protections apply ([Git operations in Git folders](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/repos/git-operations-with-repos)).

questions.title: Benefit of Git Folders Over Notebook Versioning
questions.question: A data engineer must decide between the built-in versioning of Databricks Notebooks and Databricks Git folders. What is one benefit of using Git folders (formerly Repos) instead?

choices.A: Databricks Git folders support the use of multiple branches
choices.B: Git folders eliminate the need for a Git provider by hosting repositories internally
choices.C: Git folders provide a visual diff tool for comparing notebook cell outputs
choices.D: Git folders automatically back up notebooks to cloud storage every 5 minutes

questions.shortAnswer: Databricks Git folders support the use of multiple branches.
questions.explanation: Built-in notebook versioning provides only a linear history of auto-saved snapshots. Git folders integrate fully with Git, enabling feature branches, pull requests, code reviews, and collaborative development workflows — essential for team-based software engineering practices.

questions.title: Syncing a Git Folder With Remote Changes
questions.question: A data engineer's colleague has pushed updates to the central Git repository. The data engineer needs to sync their Databricks Git folder with these changes. Which Git operation accomplishes this?

choices.A: Clone
choices.B: Pull
choices.C: Rebase
choices.D: Fetch

questions.shortAnswer: Pull.
questions.explanation: A `git pull` fetches changes from the remote repository and merges them into the current local branch. In a Databricks Git folder, this is the **Pull** action in the Git dialog (pull also clears notebook state), keeping the local copy synchronized with the latest upstream changes.

questions.title: Committing From a Git Folder *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A data engineer has edited two notebooks in a Databricks Git folder on branch `feature/dedup`. How do they get the changes to the remote repository from the workspace UI?

choices.A: Export the notebooks as DBC files and upload them to the Git provider
choices.B: Run `databricks bundle deploy`
choices.C: Open the Git dialog, select the changes, enter a commit message, and click Commit & Push
choices.D: Click Pull, which pushes local changes automatically

questions.shortAnswer: Open the Git dialog, select the changes, enter a commit message, and click Commit & Push.
questions.explanation: In Git folders, the UI "commits and pushes in a single action", and a commit message is required. Pull brings remote changes **in**. Bundle deploy pushes to a workspace, not to Git ([Git operations in Git folders](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/repos/git-operations-with-repos)).

questions.title: Creating a Feature Branch *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Before starting new work, an engineer wants a separate branch based on `main` in their Git folder. What should they do?

choices.A: Rename the `main` branch in the Git dialog
choices.B: Clone the repository again into a new workspace folder
choices.C: Ask an admin to create the branch with the Repos API
choices.D: Use the Git dialog's Create Branch option, name the branch, and choose `main` as the base

questions.shortAnswer: Use the Git dialog's Create Branch option, name the branch, and choose `main` as the base.
questions.explanation: Git folders create and switch branches from the Git dialog. Switching branches can carry uncommitted changes over. It can also delete workspace assets that don't exist on the target branch, and recreate them with new IDs when you switch back ([Git operations in Git folders](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/repos/git-operations-with-repos)).

questions.title: Reset in a Git Folder *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: An engineer clicks **Reset** on a branch in a Git folder. What is the effect?

choices.A: It is equivalent to `git reset --hard` plus `git push --force`, so committed and uncommitted changes are lost locally and on the remote branch
choices.B: Only uncommitted local changes are discarded
choices.C: The branch is restored from notebook revision history
choices.D: The Git folder is unlinked from the remote repository

questions.shortAnswer: It is equivalent to `git reset --hard` plus `git push --force`, so committed and uncommitted changes are lost locally and on the remote branch.
questions.explanation: The docs warn: "When you reset, you lose all uncommitted and committed changes in both the local and remote version of the branch." Use it only when you really want to discard work ([Git operations in Git folders](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/repos/git-operations-with-repos)).

questions.title: Keeping a Secret Out of the Bundle *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Declarative Automation Bundle deploys a job that needs a database password. The password must not appear in `databricks.yml`, in notebooks, or in Git. The CI system stores it as a secret. How should the bundle receive it at deploy time?

choices.A: Put the password in the variable's `default`
choices.B: Declare a bundle variable with no default, and have CI export `BUNDLE_VAR_<variable_name>` from its secret store
choices.C: Store it in a `passwords.txt` file in the bundle root
choices.D: Hard-code it with `spark.conf.set` in the notebook

questions.shortAnswer: Declare a bundle variable with no default, and have CI export `BUNDLE_VAR_<variable_name>` from its secret store.
questions.explanation: Bundle variables can be set from `BUNDLE_VAR_`-prefixed environment variables, so the value never enters source control. Runtime credentials can also be read in code with `dbutils.secrets.get` ([bundle variables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/variables)).

questions.title: Bundle Variable Precedence *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A bundle declares `catalog` with `default: dev`. The `prod` target sets `variables: {catalog: prod}`. In CI, the environment has `BUNDLE_VAR_catalog=staging`, and the command is `databricks bundle deploy -t prod --var="catalog=prod_v2"`. Which value is used?

choices.A: `dev`
choices.B: `prod`
choices.C: `prod_v2`
choices.D: `staging`

questions.shortAnswer: `prod_v2`.
questions.explanation: The CLI uses the first source that provides a value, in this order: the `--var` option, then `BUNDLE_VAR_` environment variables, then `variable-overrides.json`, then target `variables`, then the declaration's `default` ([bundle variables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/variables)).

questions.title: Promoting One Codebase Across Environments *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A team wants the same job definition deployed to dev, test, and prod workspaces, each writing to a different Unity Catalog catalog. What is the bundle-native approach?

choices.A: Copy `resources/job.yml` into three folders, one per environment
choices.B: Edit the job in each workspace UI after deployment
choices.C: Create three Git repositories
choices.D: Define `dev`, `test`, and `prod` targets with their own workspace hosts, and override a `catalog` variable per target

questions.shortAnswer: Define `dev`, `test`, and `prod` targets with their own workspace hosts, and override a `catalog` variable per target.
questions.explanation: Targets override top-level settings (workspace, `run_as`, variables, resource settings) per environment, so one set of resource YAML is promoted with `databricks bundle deploy -t <target>`. Manual UI edits drift from source control, and the next deploy can overwrite them ([Declarative Automation Bundles](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/)).

questions.title: Development Mode Behaviour *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: An engineer deploys a bundle with `-t dev`, where the target has `mode: development`. The deployed job never runs on its daily schedule. Why?

choices.A: Development mode pauses schedules and triggers on deployed resources, and prefixes resource names with `[dev <user>]`
choices.B: Development mode deletes schedules from the YAML
choices.C: Development mode requires a service principal
choices.D: The `dev` target always deploys to a read-only workspace

questions.shortAnswer: Development mode pauses schedules and triggers on deployed resources, and prefixes resource names with `[dev <user>]`.
questions.explanation: `mode: development` also marks pipelines as `development: true` and allows concurrent runs, so engineers can iterate safely. Run the job manually with `databricks bundle run`, or deploy to a production-mode target for scheduled runs ([deployment modes](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/deployment-modes)).

questions.title: Production Mode Safeguards *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which behaviour is part of `mode: production` for a bundle target?

choices.A: It pauses all schedules after deployment
choices.B: It validates the configured Git branch and that `run_as` and permissions are specified (a service principal is recommended), and it disallows cluster overrides
choices.C: It prefixes every resource name with the deployer's user name
choices.D: It skips YAML validation for faster deploys

questions.shortAnswer: It validates the configured Git branch and that `run_as` and permissions are specified (a service principal is recommended), and it disallows cluster overrides.
questions.explanation: Production mode also checks that pipelines are `development: false` and that paths aren't overridden to a specific user. The branch check can be overridden with `--force` ([deployment modes](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/bundles/deployment-modes)).

questions.title: Validating Before Deploying *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: In a CI pipeline, which Databricks CLI command checks that the bundle configuration is syntactically correct before anything is deployed?

choices.A: `databricks bundle sync`
choices.B: `databricks bundle destroy`
choices.C: `databricks bundle validate`
choices.D: `databricks jobs list`

questions.shortAnswer: `databricks bundle validate`.
questions.explanation: `validate` checks the bundle configuration. `deploy -t <target>` deploys it, `run` runs a job or pipeline, `plan` shows the deployment plan, and `destroy` deletes previously deployed resources ([bundle command group](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/bundle-commands)).

questions.title: Running a Bundle Job From CI *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: After `databricks bundle deploy -t test`, the CI pipeline must start the bundle's `orders_job` in the test environment and wait for the result. Which command does this?

choices.A: `databricks bundle init orders_job`
choices.B: `databricks bundle deploy orders_job --run`
choices.C: `databricks bundle summary -t test`
choices.D: `databricks bundle run orders_job -t test`

questions.shortAnswer: `databricks bundle run orders_job -t test`.
questions.explanation: `bundle run` runs "a job, pipeline, app, or script" defined in the bundle, against the selected target. `summary` lists the bundle's identity and deployed resources, and `init` creates a bundle from a template ([bundle command group](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/bundle-commands)).

questions.title: Bringing an Existing Job Under a Bundle *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A job was built by hand in the UI. The team wants it managed by their bundle without recreating it from scratch. Which CLI commands help?

choices.A: `databricks bundle generate` to produce YAML for the existing job, then `databricks bundle deployment bind` to link the bundle resource to it
choices.B: `databricks bundle destroy`, then recreate it in the UI
choices.C: `databricks bundle sync`, which copies the workspace job into Git
choices.D: `databricks bundle validate --import`

questions.shortAnswer: `databricks bundle generate` to produce YAML for the existing job, then `databricks bundle deployment bind` to link the bundle resource to it.
questions.explanation: `generate` creates bundle configuration for a resource that already exists in the workspace. `deployment bind` links a bundle-defined resource to the existing remote resource, so later deploys update it instead of creating a duplicate. `sync` is a one-way copy of local files to the workspace ([bundle command group](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/cli/bundle-commands)).

questions.title: What a Bundle Packages *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which set of assets can a Declarative Automation Bundle define and deploy together?

choices.A: Only notebooks
choices.B: Lakeflow Jobs, Lakeflow (Declarative) Pipelines, and other workspace assets such as dashboards, alongside their source code
choices.C: Only Unity Catalog grants
choices.D: Only cluster policies

questions.shortAnswer: Lakeflow Jobs, Lakeflow (Declarative) Pipelines, and other workspace assets such as dashboards, alongside their source code.
questions.explanation: A bundle is YAML configuration (`databricks.yml` plus included resource files) and the code it references, versioned in Git and deployed per target. Newer CLI versions also support resources such as Genie Agents and Lakebase projects ([bundles release notes](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/dev-tools/bundles)).

questions.title: OPTIMIZE for File Compaction
questions.question: A data engineer has discovered that the data files related to a Delta table are quite small. They aim to merge these small files into larger ones to enhance performance. Which keywords can be utilized to compact the small files?

choices.A: VACUUM
choices.B: COMPACT
choices.C: OPTIMIZE
choices.D: DEFRAGMENT

questions.shortAnswer: `OPTIMIZE`.
questions.explanation: The `OPTIMIZE` command compacts small files in a Delta table into larger ones, improving read performance by reducing the number of files that need to be scanned. This is different from `VACUUM`, which removes old data files no longer referenced by the transaction log.

questions.title: Webhook Alert for NULL Count
questions.question: A data engineer uses a Databricks SQL dashboard to monitor data quality. When the count of NULL values in a query result reaches 100, the entire team should be alerted via a messaging webhook. What method accomplishes this?

choices.A: Configure a SQL warehouse event hook that triggers on query result thresholds
choices.B: Add a conditional formatting rule to the dashboard visualization that sends a webhook
choices.C: Create a Databricks Job that polls the query results and calls the webhook via Python
choices.D: Set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination

questions.shortAnswer: Set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.
questions.explanation: Databricks SQL Alerts monitor query results against a threshold condition and trigger notifications when the condition is met. Webhook destinations allow alerts to be sent to external messaging services (Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty) in real-time.

questions.title: Diagnosing a Slow Job Task
questions.question: A single Job executes two notebooks as distinct tasks. One notebook is performing slowly during the current Job run. What method can a tech lead use to diagnose the cause?

choices.A: Navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI and click on the active run to review the processing notebook
choices.B: Check the Databricks SQL query history for slow-running queries
choices.C: Review the cluster event log for resource allocation errors
choices.D: Open the Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines pipeline UI to inspect per-table processing metrics

questions.shortAnswer: Navigate to the Runs tab in the Jobs UI and click on the active run to review the processing notebook.
questions.explanation: Clicking into the active run opens a live view of the notebook execution, including links to the Spark UI for the current task. This allows inspection of active stages, task metrics, shuffle data, and memory usage to identify performance bottlenecks.

questions.title: Job Failure Email Notification
questions.question: What approach should be taken to email the owner of a Databricks Job if it fails?

choices.A: Write a try/except block in the notebook that sends an email on failure
choices.B: Set up an Alert in the Job's notification settings (Job page)
choices.C: Configure an external monitoring tool to watch the Jobs API for failure status
choices.D: Create a downstream task that runs only on failure and sends the email

questions.shortAnswer: Set up an Alert in the Job's notification settings (Job page).
questions.explanation: Databricks Jobs support email notifications for job events (failure, success, or start). The job owner's email address is added directly from the Job's "Notifications" section, requiring no custom code or external alerting systems.

questions.title: Webhook Alert for Zero-Sales Stores
questions.question: A data engineer tracks store-level records where sales equal zero. When this count exceeds zero, the entire team should be notified via a messaging webhook. What approach accomplishes this?

choices.A: Configure a Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines expectation that triggers a webhook when zero-sales records appear
choices.B: Build a custom Python script that polls the query results and posts to the webhook
choices.C: Set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination
choices.D: Add a dashboard filter that highlights zero-sales stores and emails the team

questions.shortAnswer: Set up an Alert with a new webhook alert destination.
questions.explanation: Configure the alert condition on the query result (value > 0) and point the destination to the team's webhook URL. Databricks SQL Alerts evaluate the query result on each refresh and trigger the webhook notification when the threshold condition is met.

questions.title: Spotting a Duration Regression *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Stakeholders say a daily Lakeflow Job "feels slower lately". Where can the engineer compare recent run durations with the historical baseline, task by task?

choices.A: The workspace admin settings
choices.B: The cluster's Environment tab in the Spark UI
choices.C: `DESCRIBE HISTORY` on the output table
choices.D: The job's Runs tab matrix view

questions.shortAnswer: The job's Runs tab matrix view.
questions.explanation: The matrix view shows one column per run, with a Run total duration row and a row per task. Bar height reflects duration, so a growing bar exposes the regression and the task responsible. History is kept for 60 days. Use `system.lakeflow` tables for longer trends ([Monitor Lakeflow Jobs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/monitor)).

questions.title: Finding the Upstream Blocker *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A job run failed. In the Graph view, three downstream tasks show **Upstream failed** and one task shows **Failed**. Where should the engineer start investigating?

choices.A: The Failed task. The Upstream failed tasks didn't run because their dependency failed
choices.B: The three Upstream failed tasks, because they're the most numerous
choices.C: The cluster event log of the last task in the DAG
choices.D: The job's schedule

questions.shortAnswer: The Failed task. The Upstream failed tasks didn't run because their dependency failed.
questions.explanation: With the default Run if (*All succeeded*), a task whose dependency fails is marked `Upstream failed`. The DAG graph shows where the failure started. Fix that task, then use **Repair run** to re-run it and its dependents ([Configure task dependencies](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/conditional-tasks)).

questions.title: Succeeded With Failures *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A job run shows the status **Succeeded with failures**. What does that mean?

choices.A: Every task failed, but the job was retried successfully
choices.B: Some tasks failed, but all leaf tasks (tasks with no downstream dependencies) succeeded
choices.C: The run succeeded, but notifications failed to send
choices.D: The run timed out after producing output

questions.shortAnswer: Some tasks failed, but all leaf tasks (tasks with no downstream dependencies) succeeded.
questions.explanation: A run's outcome is determined by its leaf tasks. For example, a failed optional branch with no downstream dependents can leave the run "Succeeded with failures" ([Monitor Lakeflow Jobs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/monitor)).

questions.title: Fixing a Timed Out Task *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A task failed with status **Timed Out** after 45 minutes. With today's data volume it needs about 60 minutes. What should the engineer change so future runs complete?

choices.A: The compute's auto termination setting
choices.B: The job's max concurrent runs
choices.C: The task's timeout, raised above 60 minutes with headroom
choices.D: The upstream dependency's Run if condition

questions.shortAnswer: The task's timeout, raised above 60 minutes with headroom.
questions.explanation: If a task doesn't finish within its configured timeout, its status is set to Timed Out. With retries configured, the timeout applies to each attempt. The run-duration *warning* threshold only raises an alert, and the other settings don't control the timeout ([Configure and edit tasks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/configure-task)).

questions.title: Skewed Aggregation With AQE Enabled *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A batch job does a `groupBy("customer_id")` aggregation. In the Spark UI, most tasks in the longest stage finish in seconds, but one runs for 12 minutes. Its shuffle read is about 10× the median. AQE is enabled with default settings. Which change most directly reduces the runtime?

choices.A: Add more workers to the cluster
choices.B: Reduce `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`
choices.C: Rely on AQE skew-join handling to split the partition
choices.D: Salt the aggregation key, then aggregate the partial results in a second pass

questions.shortAnswer: Salt the aggregation key, then aggregate the partial results in a second pass.
questions.explanation: One hot key overloads a single task. AQE splits skewed partitions only in sort-merge and shuffle-hash **joins**, not in `groupBy` aggregations. More workers leave the giant task on one core, and fewer shuffle partitions make partitions bigger. Salting spreads the hot key across many tasks ([Skew and spill](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/spark-ui-guide/long-spark-stage-page), [AQE](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/aqe)).

questions.title: Diagnosing Disk Spill *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A join stage shows large **Spill (Disk)** values and high peak execution memory, with no single straggler task. Which change addresses the cause?

choices.A: Set `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` to `auto` (or more partitions), or use workers with more memory
choices.B: Disable AQE
choices.C: Increase `spark.default.parallelism` only
choices.D: Run `VACUUM` on the input tables

questions.shortAnswer: Set `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` to `auto` (or more partitions), or use workers with more memory.
questions.explanation: Spill happens when Spark runs low on execution memory during shuffles, joins, sorts, or aggregations. Smaller partitions, less data held per task, or more executor memory reduce it. `spark.default.parallelism` affects RDDs. `VACUUM` doesn't touch execution memory ([Skew and spill](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/spark-ui-guide/long-spark-stage-page)).

questions.title: Liquid Clustering Keys *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A team's Delta table uses Liquid Clustering on `event_date`. Query patterns change, and most queries now filter on `customer_id`. What should they do?

choices.A: Rewrite the table with `PARTITIONED BY (customer_id)`
choices.B: Run `ALTER TABLE t CLUSTER BY (customer_id)`, then run `OPTIMIZE` (use `OPTIMIZE ... FULL` to recluster existing data)
choices.C: Run `OPTIMIZE t ZORDER BY (customer_id)`
choices.D: Drop and recreate the table, because clustering keys can't change

questions.shortAnswer: Run `ALTER TABLE t CLUSTER BY (customer_id)`, then run `OPTIMIZE` (use `OPTIMIZE ... FULL` to recluster existing data).
questions.explanation: Clustering keys can change at any time without an immediate rewrite. Later `OPTIMIZE` runs and writes use the new keys, and `OPTIMIZE FULL` reclusters all existing data. Clustering isn't compatible with partitioning or `ZORDER` ([liquid clustering](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/clustering)).

questions.title: Automatic Liquid Clustering *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A team wants Databricks to choose and evolve clustering keys from actual query patterns. What do they need?

choices.A: Partitioning by every filter column
choices.B: `ZORDER BY AUTO` in a nightly `OPTIMIZE` job
choices.C: `CLUSTER BY AUTO` on a Unity Catalog managed table with predictive optimization enabled
choices.D: A Spark configuration that enables auto clustering on external tables

questions.shortAnswer: `CLUSTER BY AUTO` on a Unity Catalog managed table with predictive optimization enabled.
questions.explanation: Automatic liquid clustering "requires predictive optimization" for key selection and clustering operations. Predictive optimization runs only on UC managed tables ([liquid clustering](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta/clustering), [predictive optimization](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/predictive-optimization)).

questions.title: What Predictive Optimization Does *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which statement about predictive optimization is correct?

choices.A: It runs `OPTIMIZE ... ZORDER BY` on all partitioned tables
choices.B: It tunes Spark configurations for every notebook session
choices.C: It applies to external tables and tables received through sharing
choices.D: It runs `OPTIMIZE`, `VACUUM`, and `ANALYZE` automatically on Unity Catalog managed tables

questions.shortAnswer: It runs `OPTIMIZE`, `VACUUM`, and `ANALYZE` automatically on Unity Catalog managed tables.
questions.explanation: Predictive optimization runs on serverless jobs compute, applies only to UC managed tables, doesn't run `ZORDER`, and can be enabled, disabled, or inherited per catalog, schema, or table. Its history is in `system.storage.predictive_optimization_operations_history` ([predictive optimization](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/predictive-optimization)).

questions.title: Cluster Fails to Start *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A classic job cluster terminates during startup with `INIT_SCRIPT_FAILURE`. What should the engineer check first?

choices.A: The init script logs, to find why the cluster-scoped script failed (path, permissions, or a failing command)
choices.B: The Spark UI Stages tab
choices.C: The job's max concurrent runs
choices.D: The Delta transaction log of the output table

questions.shortAnswer: The init script logs, to find why the cluster-scoped script failed (path, permissions, or a failing command).
questions.explanation: `INIT_SCRIPT_FAILURE` means a cluster-scoped init script couldn't load or exited non-zero. The Spark UI doesn't exist yet because Spark never started. Other startup codes point to cloud capacity, quota, or subnet issues ([termination error codes](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/troubleshooting/cluster-error-codes)).

questions.title: Library Conflict on Shared Compute *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Two notebooks on the same all-purpose cluster need different versions of a Python library. A compute-scoped install of one version breaks the other notebook. What is the recommended fix?

choices.A: Install both versions as compute-scoped libraries
choices.B: Install each version with notebook-scoped `%pip install pkg==x.y` in the notebook that needs it
choices.C: Install the library with a global init script
choices.D: Copy the library files to DBFS root

questions.shortAnswer: Install each version with notebook-scoped `%pip install pkg==x.y` in the notebook that needs it.
questions.explanation: Notebook-scoped libraries take precedence over compute-scoped libraries, which take precedence over Runtime built-ins, and they apply only to that notebook session. Databricks doesn't recommend installing libraries with init scripts, and DBFS library storage is deprecated ([Install libraries](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/libraries/)).

questions.title: Driver Out of Memory *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A notebook crashes with a driver `OutOfMemoryError` on `pdf = spark.table("events").toPandas()`, where `events` has 300 million rows. Adding workers didn't help. What is the right fix?

choices.A: Increase `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`
choices.B: Add even more workers
choices.C: Aggregate or filter in Spark and collect only the small result (or write results to a table)
choices.D: Enable autoscaling on the cluster

questions.shortAnswer: Aggregate or filter in Spark and collect only the small result (or write results to a table).
questions.explanation: `toPandas()` and `collect()` pull every row into driver memory. Workers add executor capacity, not driver memory. Raising `spark.driver.memory` at compute level is a last resort. The real fix is to keep large data distributed ([Spark configuration: driver memory](https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html)).

questions.title: Job Failure Rate Across the Workspace *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A platform team wants a weekly dashboard of failure rates for every Lakeflow Job over the past 90 days. Which source fits best?

choices.A: The driver logs of the last run
choices.B: Each job's matrix view, screenshotted weekly
choices.C: `DESCRIBE HISTORY` on each job's output tables
choices.D: The `system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline` system table

questions.shortAnswer: The `system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline` system table.
questions.explanation: Job run system tables record runs and their result states across the account and can be queried with SQL for dashboards. The UI keeps run history for 60 days, and system tables aren't meant for real-time alerting ([System tables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/), [Monitor Lakeflow Jobs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/jobs/monitor)).

questions.title: External Table Data Retention After DROP
questions.question: A data engineer drops `my_table` with `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS my_table`. The object no longer appears in `SHOW TABLES`, but the data files still exist on the filesystem. What explains this?

choices.A: The table was an external table
choices.B: The table had active streaming readers that prevented file deletion
choices.C: The DROP command failed silently due to insufficient permissions
choices.D: The VACUUM command needs to be run separately to remove data files

questions.shortAnswer: The table was an external table.
questions.explanation: When an external table is dropped, Databricks removes only the metadata entry from the metastore. The underlying data files are stored at a user-defined location and are not managed by Databricks, so they remain intact after the table is dropped.

questions.title: Default Schema Location in the Legacy Hive Metastore
questions.question:
In a workspace still using the legacy `hive_metastore` catalog, a data engineer has established a new database with this command:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS customer360;
```

Where will the `customer360` database be situated?

choices.A: `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/`
choices.B: `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/customer360.db`
choices.C: `dbfs:/databricks/databases/customer360/`
choices.D: `dbfs:/mnt/default/customer360.db`

questions.shortAnswer: `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/customer360.db`
questions.explanation: When a database is created without specifying a `LOCATION`, Databricks stores it in the default Hive warehouse directory at `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/`. A subdirectory named `<database_name>.db` is automatically created for it. Specifying only `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse` (without the `.db` suffix) is incorrect — that is the parent warehouse directory, not the database's own location.

questions.title: DESCRIBE DATABASE Location
questions.question: Which command retrieves the location of the `customer360` database?

choices.A: `SHOW DATABASE LOCATION customer360;`
choices.B: `SELECT location FROM information_schema.databases WHERE name = 'customer360';`
choices.C: `DESCRIBE DATABASE customer360;`
choices.D: `LIST DATABASE customer360;`

questions.shortAnswer: `DESCRIBE DATABASE customer360;`
questions.explanation: This command returns database metadata including the storage location path, owner, comment, and custom properties. It is the standard way to inspect database-level information in Spark SQL and Databricks.

questions.title: Managed Table File Deletion After DROP
questions.question: A data engineer drops `my_table` and observes that both data files and metadata files are deleted from the filesystem. What explains the complete deletion?

choices.A: The VACUUM command was automatically triggered after the DROP
choices.B: The table was stored in a temporary storage location
choices.C: The table had a retention policy set to zero days
choices.D: The table was a managed table

questions.shortAnswer: The table was a managed table.
questions.explanation: When a managed (internal) table is dropped, Databricks deletes both the metastore entry and the underlying data files, because Databricks controls the full lifecycle of managed table data. This is the opposite behavior from external tables. In Unity Catalog, a dropped managed table can be recovered with `UNDROP TABLE` for 7 days by default, and the data files are deleted after that recovery period.

questions.title: Table Ownership Transfer
questions.question: A data engineer has left the organization and no longer has access. The team must transfer ownership of the engineer's Unity Catalog tables to the new lead data engineer. Who can perform this transfer?

choices.A: A metastore admin, or the owner of the tables' parent schema (or a user with MANAGE on the tables)
choices.B: Any user with SELECT privilege on the tables
choices.C: The new lead data engineer, by running `ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO` on their own
choices.D: Any member of the data team with MODIFY privilege

questions.shortAnswer: A metastore admin, or the owner of the tables' parent schema (or a user with MANAGE on the tables).
questions.explanation: In Unity Catalog, ownership can be transferred by the current owner, a metastore admin, the owner of the container (the schema for a table), or a user with the `MANAGE` privilege on the object. `SELECT` and `MODIFY` don't allow it. Use `ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO <principal>` or the Owner field in Catalog Explorer ([Manage privileges](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/)).

questions.title: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES on a Database
questions.question: A new data engineering team needs full privileges on the `customers` database to manage the project effectively. Which command grants all permissions?

choices.A: `GRANT FULL ACCESS ON DATABASE customers TO team;`
choices.B: `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE customers TO team;`
choices.C: `GRANT READ, WRITE, ADMIN ON DATABASE customers TO team;`
choices.D: `GRANT MANAGE ON DATABASE customers TO team;`

questions.shortAnswer: `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE customers TO team;`
questions.explanation: `DATABASE` is a synonym for `SCHEMA`. `ALL PRIVILEGES` grants every applicable privilege on the schema and its objects. In Unity Catalog it does **not** include `MANAGE` (or `EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA` / `EXTERNAL USE LOCATION` / `READ METADATA`), so it isn't the same as ownership.

questions.title: Discovering Tables Without Reading Data
questions.question: A newly formed data engineering team needs to discover which tables exist in the Unity Catalog catalog `customers` and view their metadata, without being able to read any data yet. Which grant fits best?

choices.A: `GRANT SELECT ON CATALOG customers TO team;`
choices.B: `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON CATALOG customers TO team;`
choices.C: `GRANT BROWSE ON CATALOG customers TO team;`
choices.D: `GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE customers TO team;`

questions.shortAnswer: `GRANT BROWSE ON CATALOG customers TO team;`
questions.explanation: `BROWSE` lets users discover objects and view metadata without usage privileges, and Databricks recommends granting it on catalogs. `SELECT` and `ALL PRIVILEGES` would expose data. `USAGE` is a legacy Hive metastore privilege. In Unity Catalog the usage privileges are `USE CATALOG` / `USE SCHEMA`, and they don't grant data access on their own ([UC privileges reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)).

questions.title: Where to Check Table Permissions
questions.question: A data engineer needs to use a Delta table but is unsure whether they have the necessary permissions. Where can they check their table permissions?

choices.A: The Databricks Admin Console under User Management
choices.B: The SQL warehouse's access control list
choices.C: The cluster configuration page under Security settings
choices.D: Catalog Explorer

questions.shortAnswer: Catalog Explorer.
questions.explanation: The Catalog Explorer in Databricks provides a dedicated "Permissions" tab for each table, listing which users and groups have access and what privilege levels are granted. It is the primary interface for inspecting and managing object-level permissions.

questions.title: Identifying a Table Owner
questions.question: A data engineer requires access to `new_table` but does not know who owns it. What method can be used to identify the owner?

choices.A: Review the Owner field in the table's page in Catalog Explorer
choices.B: Check the cluster logs for the user who last wrote to the table
choices.C: Query the `information_schema.tables` view for the table's creator
choices.D: Run `SHOW GRANT ON TABLE new_table` to list all privilege holders

questions.shortAnswer: Review the Owner field in the table's page in Catalog Explorer.
questions.explanation: Catalog Explorer displays the table owner in the table details panel. Any user with workspace access can view this field without needing special permissions, making it the standard way to identify who to contact for permission requests.

questions.title: Undoing an External-to-Managed Conversion *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A data engineer converted an external table to a Unity Catalog managed table with `ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED`. Two days later, the team must undo it. What should they run?

choices.A: `RESTORE TABLE ... TO VERSION AS OF` the version before the conversion
choices.B: `ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED`
choices.C: Drop the table and recreate it as external, because rollback isn't supported
choices.D: `ALTER TABLE ... SET EXTERNAL`

questions.shortAnswer: `ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED`.
questions.explanation: Rollback is supported within **14 days** of conversion. `UNSET MANAGED` points the table metadata back to the original external location and preserves writes made after conversion. Streams must be restarted, and Databricks deletes the managed copy seven days after rollback. `RESTORE` restores data versions, not the table type ([Convert to managed tables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/convert-external-managed)).

questions.title: Converting an External Table to Managed *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Which command converts an existing Unity Catalog external Delta table to a managed table while keeping its name, permissions, and history?

choices.A: `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t AS SELECT * FROM t`
choices.B: `CONVERT TO DELTA t`
choices.C: `ALTER TABLE t SET MANAGED` on Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS+ or serverless
choices.D: `ALTER TABLE t SET LOCATION NULL`

questions.shortAnswer: `ALTER TABLE t SET MANAGED` on Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS+ or serverless.
questions.explanation: The conversion copies data and the transaction log to managed storage, then switches metadata, with only brief writer downtime. It keeps the name, settings, permissions, views, and history. You must own the table, and existing streams must be restarted afterwards ([Convert to managed tables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/convert-external-managed)).

questions.title: Recovering a Dropped Managed Table *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A Unity Catalog managed table was dropped by mistake yesterday. What can the team do?

choices.A: Nothing, because managed-table data is deleted immediately
choices.B: Recreate it with `CREATE TABLE ... LOCATION` pointing at the old path
choices.C: Run `RESTORE TABLE` on the dropped name
choices.D: Run `UNDROP TABLE` within the recovery period (7 days by default)

questions.shortAnswer: Run `UNDROP TABLE` within the recovery period (7 days by default).
questions.explanation: Dropped managed tables can be recovered with `UNDROP TABLE` for 7 days by default, and the data files are deleted when the recovery period expires. Dropping an external table removes only metadata, and its files stay in cloud storage ([UC managed tables](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/managed)).

questions.title: DENY in Unity Catalog *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: An admin runs `DENY SELECT ON TABLE prod.gold.revenue TO contractors` in a Unity Catalog catalog, and the statement fails. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: The classic `DENY` statement applies only to the legacy `hive_metastore` catalog. In Unity Catalog, remove access by revoking (or not granting) `SELECT`, and use filters, masks, or ABAC for partial access
choices.B: The syntax is wrong. It should be `DENY SELECT TO contractors ON prod.gold.revenue`
choices.C: `DENY` works only on schemas, not tables
choices.D: `DENY` requires a metastore admin, and a workspace admin can't run it

questions.shortAnswer: The classic `DENY` statement applies only to the legacy `hive_metastore` catalog. In Unity Catalog, remove access by revoking (or not granting) `SELECT`, and use filters, masks, or ABAC for partial access.
questions.explanation: The DENY reference states it "is not supported by Unity Catalog". Unity Catalog's deny mechanism is the ABAC DENY policy (Beta), which currently denies only `MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL` ([DENY](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/security-deny), [ABAC DENY policies](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/abac/deny-policies)).

questions.title: Minimum Privileges for One Table *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: The `auditors` group must query only `prod.finance.ledger`, not the other tables in `prod.finance`. Which grants are required?

choices.A: `SELECT` on the table only
choices.B: `USE CATALOG` on `prod`, `USE SCHEMA` on `prod.finance`, and `SELECT` on `prod.finance.ledger`
choices.C: `SELECT` on schema `prod.finance`
choices.D: `ALL PRIVILEGES` on catalog `prod`

questions.shortAnswer: `USE CATALOG` on `prod`, `USE SCHEMA` on `prod.finance`, and `SELECT` on `prod.finance.ledger`.
questions.explanation: The usage privileges are required to reach objects inside a catalog or schema, but they don't grant data access by themselves. A schema-level `SELECT` would be inherited by every current and future table in the schema, which is too broad here ([UC privileges](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)).

questions.title: Masking a Column by Group *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Only members of `finance_team` may see full values in `credit_card_number`. Everyone else should see a masked value, and everyone queries the same table. What should be implemented?

choices.A: `DENY SELECT` on the column for everyone except `finance_team`
choices.B: A separate copy of the table per group
choices.C: A column mask function using `is_account_group_member('finance_team')`, attached with `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN credit_card_number SET MASK`
choices.D: Cloud IAM permissions on the column

questions.shortAnswer: A column mask function using `is_account_group_member('finance_team')`, attached with `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN credit_card_number SET MASK`.
questions.explanation: A column mask is a SQL UDF that receives the value and returns either the original or a masked value, evaluated per query. Its return type must match the column type. Copies drift, and `DENY` isn't a Unity Catalog column-level mechanism ([row filters and column masks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/row-and-column-filters)).

questions.title: Row-Level Security *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: Regional sales managers must see only the rows of `main.silver.orders` for their own region. Which implementation fits?

choices.A: `REVOKE SELECT` from all managers
choices.B: A column mask on `region`
choices.C: Partition the table by region and grant `SELECT` per partition
choices.D: A row filter UDF returning `BOOLEAN` that checks group membership against `region`, attached with `ALTER TABLE main.silver.orders SET ROW FILTER fn ON (region)`

questions.shortAnswer: A row filter UDF returning `BOOLEAN` that checks group membership against `region`, attached with `ALTER TABLE main.silver.orders SET ROW FILTER fn ON (region)`.
questions.explanation: Rows for which the row filter returns `FALSE` are excluded from results. Masks change column values, not row visibility, and Unity Catalog doesn't grant privileges per partition ([row filters and column masks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/tables/row-and-column-filters)).

questions.title: Masking PII Across Many Tables *(2026 blueprint)*
questions.question: A privacy team must mask every email column in all tables of the `main.silver` schema, including tables created later. Table owners must not be able to remove the masking. What should they use?

choices.A: A Unity Catalog ABAC column mask policy on the schema, matching columns tagged with a governed tag such as `pii = email`
choices.B: A column mask set separately on each table by its owner
choices.C: A dynamic view per table
choices.D: An ABAC DENY policy on `SELECT`

questions.shortAnswer: A Unity Catalog ABAC column mask policy on the schema, matching columns tagged with a governed tag such as `pii = email`.
questions.explanation: ABAC policies (`CREATE POLICY ... COLUMN MASK ... FOR TABLES MATCH COLUMNS has_tag_value('pii','email')`) attach at catalog, schema, or table level and apply automatically to objects with matching governed tags. Because higher-level admins define them, table owners can't override or remove them. DENY policies currently deny only `MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL` ([ABAC](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/abac/), [ABAC policies](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/abac/policies)).
